_about: Protocol-by-protocol compatibility, 26 Nov 2026. 'joins': is a combination defined in either spec. 'wild': is the pair seen together (live = generally available product, verified at the vendor's own page on 26 Nov 2026; announced = announced, documented, preview or pilot; code = both in one GitHub package manifest). 'alternatives': same-job pairs. 'keys': algorithms each spec allows for the agent or payer key (used in compatibility.md). Evidence: compatibility-profiles.json, evidence-vendor-stacks.md, evidence-code-cooccurrence.md.

MCP.basis: No agent signing key in core; private_key_jwt is a MAY with no algorithm set

x401.basis: No agent signing key; algorithms delegated to OpenID4VP and the DC API

A2A.basis: Agent Card JWS alg unrestricted (ES256, RS256 are examples)

WebBotAuth.basis: Any IANA-registered RFC 9421 algorithm; no mandatory-to-implement algorithm; HMAC forbidden

TAP.basis: No algorithm mandated; examples Ed25519, sample code also rsa-pss-sha256; keys held by Visa's key service

ACP.basis: Request signature algorithm agreed out-of-band (examples Ed25519, ES256)

AP2.basis: Agent key is an RFC 7800 cnf JWK, algorithm not restricted (examples P-256)

UCP.basis: Verifiers MUST support ES256; ES384 and EdDSA OPTIONAL

VI.basis: ES256 MUST at every layer; EdDSA deferred

PAP.basis: Session JWT alg MUST be ES256 (client assertions and delegations ES256 or PS384)

KYA-OS.basis: Ed25519 for all operations in core (did:key is Ed25519); Entity Card per-request proof allows EdDSA or ES256

x402.basis: Payer key: EIP-712 on EVM, Ed25519 on Solana and TON; optional HTTP message signatures extension has no algorithm restriction

MPP.basis: Per payment method: EIP-712 (secp256k1), Tempo (secp256k1, P-256, WebAuthn), Solana and NEAR (Ed25519)

ERC8004.basis: EIP-712 from an Ethereum account; ERC-1271 contract wallets can verify other schemes

notes.1: PAP and KYA-OS look unlikely to share the agent's delegated key as written. PAP's Session JWT must be ES256, while KYA-OS's core did:key delegate is Ed25519; KYA-OS allows ES256 only for its Entity Card per-request proof. An agent would probably need two keys, linked in a way neither spec currently describes.
notes.2: Visa TAP and Web Bot Auth both build on RFC 9421, but a Web Bot Auth verifier following draft-01 is unlikely to accept a TAP signature as is: TAP uses different tags (agent-browser-auth, agent-payer-auth), sends no Signature-Agent, publishes keys through Visa's key service, and adds a nonce and an 8-minute window.
notes.3: UCP and AP2 are linked by UCP's optional AP2 Mandates extension, but there appear to be seams: UCP signs a checkout object with a detached JWS where AP2 expects a checkout JWT; UCP has no obvious field for AP2's receipts; and AP2's documents differ on whether Ed25519 may sign the checkout.
notes.4: PAP recommends that operators sign with Web Bot Auth, but a valid Web Bot Auth signature does not on its own show that the signer is PAP's client_id: the two key sources are separate and both self-published.
notes.5: UCP's documented Web Bot Auth example adds a type parameter to Signature-Agent, which draft-01 says a verifier must ignore. They should still interoperate where Signature-Agent points at a bare JWK Set URL, which UCP allows.
notes.6: KYA-OS and Web Bot Auth look technically compatible: both identify keys by the RFC 7638 thumbprint, and Web Bot Auth allows Ed25519. Neither spec describes the join yet.
notes.7: x402 describes an MCP transport, but we found nothing that ties the paying wallet to the MCP caller.
notes.8: Verifiable Intent and AP2 0.2 cover much the same mandate layer, so in most designs they would be alternatives rather than layers.
notes.9: The link between ERC-8004 and x402 appears weak: an optional proofOfPayment transaction hash in the off-chain feedback file, given as an example. The registry does not check it, and we found no mention of ERC-8004 in the x402 repository.
notes.10: A PAP and AP2 join has been proposed in an open PAP issue (#61) but not yet specified. The keys look compatible: PAP's delegated key and AP2's cnf key are both P-256.
notes.11: UCP verifiers are only required to support ES256 (EdDSA is optional), so a KYA-OS core Ed25519 signature may not be accepted by every conformant UCP verifier.
